what: How each North Carolina place voted in six contests of the 2020, 2022 and 2024 general elections: the votes for the Democratic candidate or ticket, the Republican candidate or ticket, everyone else together (write-ins included) and the total, added up from the North Carolina State Board of Elections' official precinct results.
note: What this is: how the people of a place voted in that election, in the State Board of Elections' official precinct results, added up here by county, by court district made of whole counties, and for 2024 by state House and Senate district on the plans enacted in 2023 and still in force for 2026. Many counties report early, mail and provisional votes in units that are not precincts; those votes are in the county's figures, and a district taking in part of such a county is left out, as is one with a precinct that lay in two districts: nothing is divided by estimate. What this is not: it is not a prediction of any election; it says nothing about any candidate on a later ballot or about any voter; a nonpartisan office stays nonpartisan; and a district's figures are for its lines of that year. North Carolina elected its Governor in 2020 and 2024 and held no contest for U.S. Senator in 2024. The candidates and tickets are named only to say which election this was. In a place with very few voters the split would come close to saying how particular people voted, so there the split is left out.

few.why: A place's too_few lists the contests in which it had fewer than 20 votes, or in which every vote went the same way. There the split comes close to saying how particular people voted, so a page should leave it out. The counts are the official record all the same, and are kept here so that the sums can be checked.

not_given: Cities and towns are not added up: North Carolina's precincts are not drawn inside town lines, and no list a script can read says which part of a precinct lies in which town, so a town's votes cannot be counted without estimating. County commissioner districts are not added up: no statewide list says which precinct lies in which, and most counties elect commissioners countywide. School boards, soil and water districts and sanitary districts are not added up as districts of their own; most school boards are elected by a whole county, whose figures are given. Congressional districts are not given here (the 2026 plan, S.L. 2025-95, was not in force at these elections).

county.note: A county's figures are every vote it reported, in its precincts and in its units that are not precincts.

house.what: State House districts of House Redistricting Plan 2023/H898 Ed 2 (S.L. 2023-149, enacted October 25, 2023), in force for 2024 and 2026
house.why_not: A district is missing where it takes in part of a county that reported early, mail or provisional votes in units that are not precincts (those votes cannot be placed in a part of the county), or where a precinct of it with votes lay in two districts: nothing is divided by estimate. The 2022 and 2020 elections were held on earlier House and Senate plans; the plans in force for 2026 were enacted in October 2023 and first used in 2024, so only 2024 is given.
house.note: A district is the whole of each county lying wholly in it, and the precincts of a divided county that reported every vote by precinct; a precinct's district is read from the district contest on its rows. Each district given was checked: its own contest, added up over the same precincts and counties, equals the Board's total for that contest.

senate.what: State Senate districts of Realign NC Senate Districts 2023/SB758,2 Ed (S.L. 2023-146, enacted October 25, 2023), in force for 2024 and 2026
senate.why_not: A district is missing where it takes in part of a county that reported early, mail or provisional votes in units that are not precincts (those votes cannot be placed in a part of the county), or where a precinct of it with votes lay in two districts: nothing is divided by estimate. The 2022 and 2020 elections were held on earlier House and Senate plans; the plans in force for 2026 were enacted in October 2023 and first used in 2024, so only 2024 is given.
senate.note: A district is the whole of each county lying wholly in it, and the precincts of a divided county that reported every vote by precinct; a precinct's district is read from the district contest on its rows. Each district given was checked: its own contest, added up over the same precincts and counties, equals the Board's total for that contest.

judicial.what: Prosecutorial, district court and superior court districts, as whole counties
judicial.why_not: A court district that takes in only part of a county (in our 2026 list, the district court districts of Wake County; the superior court districts of Cumberland County, Guilford County, Mecklenburg County, Wake County) is not given: the results are not added up for parts of a county.
